en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on the All-Knowing Wisdom within the Section of Puzzling Questions.
3. The Question on the Gravity and Lightness of Intentional Lying “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘In the case of intentional lying, one is defeated (pārājika).’”
But it is also said:
"One incurs a light offense for a deliberate lie, the basis of which is confession in the presence of one person.
Venerable Nāgasena, what is the distinction here, and what is the reason that by one instance of lying one is ruined, while by another instance of lying one remains curable?
“Venerable Nāgasena, if it was said by the Blessed One:

‘One who speaks a deliberate lie commits a pārājika offense,’ then that statement which says, ‘In the case of a deliberate lie, one incurs a light offense, the basis for which is confession before a single person,’ must be false.
If it was indeed spoken by the Tathāgata—”

“If it is said that one incurs a light offense for a deliberate lie, which is to be confessed in the presence of a single person, then the statement that ‘one becomes defeated (pārājika) by a deliberate lie’ must also be false.
This too is a double-edged question that has come to you; it must be resolved by you.
“It was indeed spoken thus, Great King, by the Blessed One:”
‘In the case of intentional lying, one is defeated.
Yet it has also been said:

‘In the case of intentional lying, one incurs a light offense, the basis for which is to be confessed in the presence of a single person. Furthermore, that [offense] is heavy or light depending on the specific matter.
“What do you think, Great King? Suppose here some man were to give another a blow with his hand; what punishment would you inflict upon him?
“If, venerable sir, he says, ‘I do not forgive him,’ then we would have a kahāpaṇa coin taken from him for his lack of forgiveness.”
“But suppose, Great King, that very same man were to strike you with his hand; what punishment would he receive?
“Venerable sir, we would have his hand cut off, we would have his foot cut off, and even his head cut off like a bamboo shoot;
we would have his entire house plundered, and both sides of his family, down to the seventh generation.”
“...we shall have them eradicated. “But what is the distinction here, Great King, and what is the reason that for one person striking with the hand the fine is a small coin,
whereas for you, for striking with the hand, there is the cutting off of hands, the cutting off of feet, up to the cutting off of the bamboo-joints, and the seizure of the entire household?”
“Is there a complete eradication of both sides back as far as the seventh generation?
“Only by means of human intervention, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, intentional lying is heavy or light depending on the basis.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! This is so; thus do I accept it.
The third dilemma, concerning the gravity or lightness of false speech.
